nodes.summary: If the cluster counts with boundary graphs `C ≤ C'` differ by at most `N`, then `φ^C(A) ≤ q^N φ^{C'}(A)` for nonnegative event indicators.
nodes.title: Boundary-graph comparison $\varphi^{C'}(A) \le q^N \varphi^C(A)$

nodes.summary: The mass `φ^C_{G,p,q}(A)` of an event under the random-cluster measure with boundary graph `C`.
nodes.title: Event mass under the random-cluster measure with a boundary graph

nodes.summary: A wiring whose edges join boundary vertices lies below the boundary clique.
nodes.title: Boundary-supported wirings lie below the boundary clique

nodes.summary: The empty wiring gives the free random-cluster measure.
nodes.title: Empty wiring gives the free random-cluster measure

nodes.summary: The boundary clique gives the wired random-cluster measure.
nodes.title: Boundary clique gives the wired random-cluster measure

nodes.summary: Holley's condition for the probabilities with nested wirings `C ≤ C'` and `q ≥ 1`.
nodes.title: Holley's condition for probabilities with nested wirings, $q \ge 1$

nodes.summary: The free lower bound together with the bound by the boundary condition `⊤` (all vertices wired).
nodes.title: Sandwich between the free and all-wired boundary conditions

nodes.summary: For `q ≥ 1` and `C` inside the boundary clique, `φ^0(A) ≤ φ^C(A) ≤ φ^1(A)` for every increasing event `A`.
nodes.title: Free–wired sandwich for boundary graphs inside the boundary clique

nodes.summary: Disintegration: `φ_C(ω)` is the mass of the fibre of `ω` times the conditional probability of `ω` in that fibre.
nodes.title: Disintegration of a boundary-wired measure over conditioning fibres

nodes.summary: Comparison of boundary conditions for the random-cluster measure: for `q ≥ 1` and wirings `C ≤ C'`, `φ_C(A) ≤ φ_C'(A)` for every increasing event `A`. This follows from Holley's inequality (Holley, 1974); see Grimmett, *The Random-Cluster Model* (2006), Chapter 4.
nodes.title: Random-cluster comparison of boundary conditions for $q \ge 1$

nodes.summary: For `q ≥ 1`, the random-cluster measure with boundary graph `C` is increasing in `p` on increasing events.
nodes.title: Boundary-graph FK measure increases in $p$ for $q \ge 1$

nodes.summary: FKG inequality for the random-cluster measure (Fortuin, Kasteleyn and Ginibre, 1971): for `q ≥ 1` and any boundary wiring `C`, increasing functions are positively correlated under `φ_C`. See Grimmett, *The Random-Cluster Model* (2006), Chapter 3.
nodes.title: FKG inequality for the random-cluster measure, $q \ge 1$

nodes.summary: The random-cluster probability with boundary wiring `C`, `bcWeight / bcZ`.
nodes.title: Random-cluster probability with a boundary wiring

nodes.summary: Holley's condition for the weights with nested wirings `C ≤ C'` and `q ≥ 1`.
nodes.title: Holley's condition for weights with nested wirings, $q \ge 1$

nodes.summary: The unnormalized random-cluster weight with boundary wiring `C`: `edgeProduct G p ω · q ^ numClustersBC G C ω`.
nodes.title: Random-cluster weight with a boundary wiring

nodes.summary: The partition function with boundary wiring `C`.
nodes.title: Partition function with a boundary wiring

nodes.summary: The number of connected components of simple graphs on a finite vertex set is supermodular: `#comp(G₁) + #comp(G₂) ≤ #comp(G₁ ⊔ G₂) + #comp(G₁ ⊓ G₂)`.
nodes.title: Supermodularity of the number of connected components

nodes.summary: The number of open edges of `G` in `ω`. Same as `openCount` in `Tilt`.
nodes.title: Number of open edges of a configuration

nodes.summary: Holley's condition for the conditional measures with nested wirings `C ≤ C'` and `q ≥ 1`.
nodes.title: Holley's condition for nested-wiring conditional measures, $q \ge 1$

nodes.summary: For `q ≥ 1` and `C ≤ C'`, the conditional measure with wiring `C` is dominated by the one with wiring `C'` on increasing events.
nodes.title: Conditional measures increase with the wiring for $q \ge 1$

nodes.summary: The random-cluster measure with wiring `C` conditioned on agreeing with `ψ` off the edge set `F`.
nodes.title: Conditional random-cluster measure with a boundary wiring

nodes.summary: The edges of `G` closed in `b` and open in `c`.
nodes.title: Edges closed in one configuration and open in another

nodes.summary: For `q ≥ 1`, every edge of `G` is open with probability between `p / (p + q(1 - p))` and `p`.
nodes.title: Edge density lies between $p/(p+q(1-p))$ and $p$ for $q \ge 1$

nodes.summary: The probability `μ(ω(e) = 1)` that the coordinate `e` is open under the mass function `μ`.
nodes.title: Edge marginal of a mass function

nodes.summary: The probability `φ_{G,p,q}(e open)` that the edge `e` is open.
nodes.title: Probability that an edge is open under the random-cluster measure

nodes.summary: Two monotonically coupled measures with the same edge marginals give the same mass to every increasing event.
nodes.title: Monotone couplings with equal edge marginals agree on up-sets

nodes.summary: The mass `μ(A)` of an event under the mass function `μ`.
nodes.title: Mass of an event under a mass function

nodes.summary: For `q ≥ 1`, `P_{p/(p + q(1 - p))} ≼ φ_{p,q} ≼ P_p`, with every law extended uniformly to loops and nonedges. On graph-edge marginals, this gives the usual FK/Bernoulli comparison (Fortuin 1972; Grimmett, *The Random-Cluster Model*, 2006, Theorem 3.21).
nodes.title: Comparison inequalities

nodes.summary: For `q ≥ 1` the random-cluster measure is stochastically increasing in `p`.
nodes.title: Random-cluster measure increases stochastically in $p$ when $q \ge 1$

nodes.summary: Holley's cross inequality for two random-cluster measures with `p₁ ≤ p₂` and the same `q ≥ 1`.
nodes.title: Holley's cross inequality for FK measures, $p_1 \le p_2$, $q \ge 1$

nodes.summary: For `q ≥ 1` and `p ∈ (0, 1)`, the random-cluster measure satisfies the FKG lattice condition `φ(a) φ(b) ≤ φ(a ⊔ b) φ(a ⊓ b)`.
nodes.title: FKG lattice condition for the random-cluster measure

nodes.summary: For `q ≥ 1` and a wiring `C` supported on the boundary, free ≤ `φ_C` ≤ wired on every increasing event.
nodes.title: Boundary wirings lie between free and wired when $q \ge 1$

nodes.summary: For `q ≥ 1` the free random-cluster measure gives every increasing event at most the probability the wired measure gives it.
nodes.title: Free–wired domination on a finite graph for $q \ge 1$

nodes.summary: The FKG inequality for increasing events: `φ(A) φ(B) ≤ φ(A ∩ B)` for `q ≥ 1`.
nodes.title: FKG inequality for increasing random-cluster events

nodes.summary: For `q ≥ 1`, increasing functions are positively correlated under `φ_{G,p,q}`: `φ(f) φ(g) ≤ φ(f g)`. (Fortuin–Kasteleyn–Ginibre, Comm. Math. Phys. 22, 1971; Grimmett, *The Random-Cluster Model*, 2006, Theorem 3.8.)
nodes.title: FKG inequality for the random-cluster model

nodes.summary: For `q ≥ 1` and `p₁ ≤ p₂`, `φ_{p₁,q}(A) ≤ φ_{p₂,q}(A)` for every increasing event `A` (Grimmett, *The Random-Cluster Model*, 2006, Theorem 3.21).
nodes.title: Monotonicity of the random-cluster measure in `p`

nodes.summary: For `q ≥ 1` the free box measure is stochastically dominated by the wired box measure on `ℤ^d`: `φ⁰_n ≼ φ¹_n`.
nodes.title: Free box measure dominated by the wired one for $q \ge 1$

nodes.summary: Holley's condition for the free and wired probabilities when `q ≥ 1`.
nodes.title: Holley's condition for free and wired probabilities when $q \ge 1$

nodes.summary: Holley's condition for the free and wired weights when `q ≥ 1`. See also `bcWeight_cross`, which contains this as the case of boundary wirings `⊥ ≤ clique`.
nodes.title: Holley's condition for free and wired weights when $q \ge 1$

nodes.summary: The partition function of the fibre of `ψ` off `F`: the sum of `bcWeight` over configurations agreeing with `ψ` off `F`.
nodes.title: Partition function of a conditioning fibre

nodes.summary: `P` is a monotone coupling of the mass functions `μ` and `ν`: a nonnegative mass function on pairs with marginals `μ` and `ν`, supported on pairs `(ω, ω')` with `ω ≤ ω'`.
nodes.title: Monotone coupling of two mass functions

nodes.summary: The kernel of the Laplacian of the open subgraph of `ω`, a subspace of `V → ℝ`.
nodes.title: Kernel of the Laplacian of the open subgraph

nodes.summary: Mixed supermodularity of cluster counts for nested wirings `C ≤ C'`: `k_C(a) + k_C'(b) ≤ k_C(a ⊓ b) + k_C'(a ⊔ b)`.
nodes.title: Mixed supermodularity of cluster counts for nested wirings

nodes.summary: Mixed supermodularity of cluster counts: `k(a) + k¹(b) ≤ k(a ⊓ b) + k¹(a ⊔ b)`, where `k¹` counts clusters with the boundary wired.
nodes.title: Mixed supermodularity of free and wired cluster counts

nodes.summary: For `b ≤ c`, `k(b) + o(b) ≤ k(c) + o(c)`: opening an edge lowers the cluster count by at most one.
nodes.title: Cluster count plus open-edge count is monotone

nodes.summary: The number of clusters of `ω` under the boundary wiring `C`: connected components of the open subgraph of `ω` joined with `C`.
nodes.title: Number of clusters under a boundary wiring

nodes.summary: The number of open clusters equals the dimension of the kernel of the Laplacian of the open subgraph.
nodes.title: Number of open clusters equals the dimension of the Laplacian kernel

nodes.summary: The cluster count of the random-cluster model is supermodular in the configuration.
nodes.title: Supermodularity of the random-cluster cluster count

nodes.summary: The reduced density `p / (p + q(1 - p))`: the Bernoulli parameter dominated by `φ_{p,q}`.
nodes.title: Reduced density $p/(p + q(1-p))$

nodes.summary: Conditional version of `wiredFkProb_inner_dominated`.
nodes.title: Wired measure conditionally dominated by larger wirings, $q \ge 1$

nodes.summary: For `q ≥ 1` the wired measure is dominated by `φ_C'` for any wiring `C'` containing the boundary clique.
nodes.title: Wirings with the boundary clique dominate the wired measure, $q \ge 1$
